sharedEvidence.morphometrics: Male/female first two PCA components explain 86.46%/79.56%; overlapping morphospace and intraspecific variation prevent stable metric-only discrimination as authors state

readEvidence.type: KIZ2015051 male, Bozhu Town, Wenshan, Yunnan, 2180 m, 16 April 2015; two additional male and five female paratypes
readEvidence.size: Diagnostic adult male SVL 83–107 mm; female 94–110 mm, overlapping ranges
readEvidence.diagnosis: Rough warted dorsum, indistinct tympanum, finger I slightly longer than II, toe III slightly longer than V, fully webbed incurved toes, tarsal fold. Adult males hypertrophied forelimbs, spines on chest, inner metacarpal and fingers I–III, internal vocal sac
readEvidence.variation: Females lack male forelimb hypertrophy and chest/inner metacarpal/fingers II–III spines but retain small finger-I spines. Wart shape and brown dorsal/orange-yellow ventral colour vary
readEvidence.locality: Known Wenshan City; other same-elevation Wenshan areas speculative
readEvidence.ecology: Night mountain-stream encounters, floating near bank or sitting on shore. No courtship calls heard, eggs or tadpoles found; breeding habits unknown

readEvidence.type: KIZ2015115 male, Tianxing Town, Daguan County, Zhaotong, Yunnan, 1920 m, 25 September 2015; two additional male and four female paratypes
readEvidence.size: Diagnostic adult male SVL 106–114 mm; female 98–103 mm; do not invert sex labels to conform to an assumed pattern
readEvidence.diagnosis: Relatively smooth dorsum with flat tubercles, relatively visible tympanum, finger I longer than II, toe III longer than V, fully webbed incurved toes, tarsal fold. Adult male forelimb hypertrophy, chest/inner metacarpal/fingers I–III spines, internal vocal sac
readEvidence.variation: Females lack male forelimb hypertrophy and described chest, metacarpal and finger spines. Flat tubercle visibility and yellow-brown dorsal colour vary
readEvidence.locality: Known Daguan County; other same-elevation Zhaotong areas speculative
readEvidence.ecology: Small-river encounters at night, floating near shore or sitting on rocks in water. No courtship calls heard, eggs or tadpoles found; breeding habits unknown
